confirmed.statement: The nine arm n_analyzed values are right. The N row of Table I reads AUT_High 76, AUT_Low 69, AUT_NoAI 68, DAT_High 84, DAT_Low 78, DAT_NoAI 83, RAT_High 106, RAT_Low 106, RAT_NoAI 105. The page image and the PDF text layer (matched to the column headers by position) give the same digits. The cells sum to 775 (AUT 213, DAT 245, RAT 317).

The counts are people, not responses or rounds. The cells sum to the 775 'participants' of Section III.D, not to 2,325 participant-rounds (three rounds each). Section IV counts participants with AI access by task as 145 (AUT), 212 (RAT), and 162 (DAT), 519 in all. These equal the High plus Low cells of Table I (76+69, 106+106, 84+78).

confirmed.statement: The n_randomized nulls (study and all nine arms) are right under form-spec rule 1 and the 'Counts in prose' note. The paper prints no count at assignment. Assignment came mid-survey, after consent, the creativity slider, the AI-attitude items, and the verbal fluency task ('At this point, participants are randomly assigned to one of the 9 experimental conditions'). confirmed.statement: The exclusions text is accurate. 185 of the 960 recruits (960 - 775) were dropped for not completing the study or failing an attention check. The paper does not say how many of them had been assigned, and it gives no exclusions by cell. The 40 pilot participants are a separate group ('different from those included in the pilot') and are not analyzed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section III.D Participants

confirmed.statement: Attrition by task (an observation, not a coding error). Within each task the three AI cells are near equal (AUT 76/69/68, DAT 84/78/83, RAT 106/106/105), but the task totals are not (213, 245, 317). Neither an equal three-way task split (chi-square 22.0, 2 df, p < .001) nor the half-RAT split that the abstract's two-step wording could imply (chi-square 28.3) fits these totals. The paper reports neither exclusions by cell nor assignment shares, so exclusions may have differed by task. Every contrast in the form compares arms within one task, and those arms are balanced. No count in the form changes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1773), Table I; PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section III.B; chi-square computed from the Table I N row

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds by a wide margin. One randomized study analyzed 775 people. Each task has at least 213, the smallest cell has 68, and the smallest full-arm contrast in the form (AUT_Low 69 vs AUT_NoAI 68) has 137.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section III.D; PDF p. 4, Table I

summary: The PDF supports every people count in the form: 960 Prolific recruits, 775 analyzed after dropping non-completers and attention-check failures, nine Table I cells of 68 to 106 people that sum to 775 and match the AI-access counts in Section IV, and null randomized counts because no count at assignment is printed. Criterion 2 holds by a wide margin in this one study, no other paper uses these people, and the only open point is unexplained attrition by task (totals 213, 245, 317 against near-equal cells within each task), which changes no count in the form.
